title: How Ski Resorts Make Snow ❄️ #shorts
description:
Ski season is here, but much of the snow on the slopes came out of a cannon. Snow guns spray a fine mist of water into cold air, using a big fan or compressed air to fling it out over the trail. As some droplets evaporate they pull heat out of the air, cooling it enough to freeze the droplets around them. Some machines add nucleating agents to help droplets freeze faster. Humidity matters as much as temperature: crews watch the wet-bulb temperature, and in very dry air they can make snow even a few degrees above freezing. Machine-made snow is denser and rounder, because each droplet has only a short drop to freeze instead of a long fall from a cloud.
